subject: physics_2
question_text: Name a physical quantity whose dimensions are the same as those of angular momentum?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: angular momentum L = mvr has dimensions [M][LT⁻¹][L] = ML²T⁻¹; Planck's constant h = E/ν has [ML²T⁻²]/[T⁻¹] = ML²T⁻¹ — the two match, which is why Bohr could set mvr = nh/2π.

recall_prompt: Say the answer you would write — the quantity you name, and how you show the dimensions match.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Name Planck's constant
lines: Planck's constant h has the same dimensions
steps.margin_note: First mark is the name. Write h with the words Planck's constant.
steps.why: Bohr's quantum condition mvr = nh/2π only makes sense because h and angular momentum have the same dimensions — that is the connection this question tests.
common_mistakes: Naming energy or momentum. Neither has the dimensions ML²T⁻¹.
Writing only the symbol h without the name.

recall.must_convey: That Planck's constant has the same dimensions as angular momentum.

steps.memory_tip: L = nh/2π — the two sides of Bohr's condition must have the same dimensions.

steps.label: The matching dimensions

lines.text: L = mvr → [M][L T⁻¹][L] = M L² T⁻¹
h = E/ν → [M L² T⁻²]/[T⁻¹] = M L² T⁻¹
Planck's constant h — dimensions M L² T⁻¹

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Show both quantities reduce to ML²T⁻¹.
steps.why: The mark is for showing the match, not asserting it: L = mvr and h = E/ν both reduce to ML²T⁻¹ when each factor is replaced by its dimensions.
common_mistakes: Writing ML²T⁻² (the dimensions of energy) instead of ML²T⁻¹.
Deriving only one side and not showing the other.

recall.must_convey: That both reduce to ML²T⁻¹, from L = mvr and h = E/ν.
accept: both are M L squared T inverse
reject: M L squared T minus two

steps.memory_tip: Energy over frequency: ML²T⁻² divided by T⁻¹ gives ML²T⁻¹.

insider_note: The name alone is half the marks — the other half needs both dimensional formulas written out to ML²T⁻¹.
